lee (support): Customer reports intermittent 401s from Console when saving an API key. Happens about 1/15-1/30 attempts. They can repro in Chrome. Asking for minimal HAR + console + curl steps we can share so they can upload a debug bundle.

alex (frontend): Ok — here’s a compact checklist to send the customer. Keep it minimal so they actually follow it. Paste as-is into the support reply.

alex (frontend): 1) Reproduce once while recording: open Chrome DevTools (F12) -> Network tab -> check “Preserve log”.
2) Also open Console tab (keep it visible).
3) Reproduce the failing action in the Console (save API key / call your endpoint).
4) Right-click on the Network list -> “Save all as HAR with content” -> name it “har-saveapi-YYYYMMDD.zip”.
5) In Console: right-click -> “Save as...” -> save as “console-saveapi-YYYYMMDD.txt”.

alex (frontend): For the curl repro: find the failed request in Network -> right click -> “Copy → Copy as cURL”. Paste into a text file. IMPORTANT: redact the Authorization header before uploading (replace token with <REDACTED_TOKEN>).

alex (frontend): Ask them to also note the exact local time (TZ) for the repro, and include the response headers for the failing request. We specifically need any header that looks like `X-Request-Id`, `X-Trace-Id`, or `Request-Id` (we use these to find the log in infra).

emma (qa): Quick additions for other browsers / mobile:
- Firefox: Network -> right click -> Save all as HAR. Console -> right click -> Save as.
- Safari (mac): Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> Export as HAR. Console -> Save as.
- iOS / Android webviews: use an HTTP proxy (Charles/Fiddler) and export the session as a .har, or ask customer to reproduce on desktop for fastest turnaround.

emma (qa): If they can't attach HAR (corp policy), ask for: exact timestamp (to the minute), the `Copy as cURL` text (with auth redacted), and the console text file. That alone is usually enough to track the request in logs.

alex (frontend): Packaging checklist to send to customer (short):
- HAR file (Save all as HAR with content)
- Console log (save as .txt)
- cURL copy (redact token)
- Short repro steps (browser, exact clicks, is Incognito used?)
- Local time window (e.g., 2026-03-15 14:07-14:10 UTC)
- If available, screenshot of the UI error and the exact error text (e.g., "401: Unauthorized - invalid session").

alex (frontend): Extra tips:
- Turn off extensions / adblockers if customer can reproduce with them on, we want both results if possible.
- If the failure is intermittent, ask them to reproduce ~5 times and keep the HAR for the first fail.
- For long requests, set Network -> Preserve log and disable “Capture screenshots” to reduce HAR size.

deploy-bot: Support ticket created: SUP-4567 for customer "Acme Corp". Attachments: none yet.

lee (support): Thanks — I pasted the checklist to the customer and requested the first failing HAR + console + curl + time window. I asked them to upload via the secure upload link in the ticket.

lee (support): Minimal internal triage notes for engineers (short):
- Look for `401` events in logs at the given time window.
- Match by `X-Request-Id` / `X-Trace-Id` if present in headers.
- Check token validation path + any auth service 5xx/timeout spikes in the window.

emma (qa): If you want to reproduce locally: use the same `Copy as cURL` command and run locally after redacting tokens and swapping in a test token. If we see the same 401, grab server-side logs around timestamp and correlate with request id.

lee (support): If customer uploads, I will add the filenames to the ticket and ping #eng-frontend with the request id and timestamp. If they can't upload, we escalate to a live screenshare.

lee (support): Thanks team — will update here when they upload. :pray:
